item.title: Resiliencia e inversión no son objetivos contrapuestos en el sector asegurador

item.title: Más de una cuarta parte de las aseguradoras prevé aumentar su reaseguro de Daños en 2027

item.title: Fundación Asisa entrega diez ayudas a proyectos de investigación en salud y acción social
item.description: Fundación Asisa ha llevado a cabo el acto de entrega de las ayudas correspondientes a su primera convocatoria de apoyo a la investigación sanitaria y a proyectos sociales. La convocatoria ha concedido diez ayudas de 6.000 euros cada una, cinco para proyectos de investigación en salud y cinco para iniciativas sociales.

item.title: Lemonade $10.5 Million Settlement Over License Number Data Breach Approved
item.description: A federal district court in New York has approved a $10.5 million class action settlement by digital insurer Lemonade over its exposing license numbers of as many as 190,644 drivers to third parties through its online auto insurance quote platform. The case consolidated complaints brought by three plaintiffs from New York, Connecticut and Arizona on behalf of themselves and others affected by the quoting platform’s data breach, even if they were not Lemonade customers and never even applied for insurance from Lemonade. The quoting feature uses the name, date of birth, and address entered by the website visitor, combined with additional information Lemonade already has or can access from third-party data brokers, and then automatically “pre-fills” the driver’s license information.

item.title: Nestle India Faces Legal Action Over Infant Formula Claims
item.description: Related: Abbott to Pay $385 Million to End US Claims Over Infant Formula FSSAI also found a sample of the firm’s follow-up formula “sub-standard” for its Biotin content, it said, adding that legal action has been initiated against Nestle India “over several non-compliances pertaining to the Food Safety and Standards Act.” Nestle shares reversed early gains to fall as much as 2.8% after the announcement compared to an advance in the benchmark Nifty 50 Index. India’s food regulator said it has initiated legal action against Nestle India Ltd. Related: Abbott to Pay $670 Million to Settle Some Preterm Infant Formula Cases Nestle has submitted a detailed response regarding statements appearing on the labels, “which are factual in nature, and supported by scientific literature,” the spokesperson said.

item.title: FCA takes Hunter Jones to High Court over alleged unauthorised activity

item.description: Ten most read articles on Artemis.bm, week ending September 20th 2026: This is not every article published on Artemis during the last week, just the most popular among our readers over the last seven days. Here are the ten most popular news articles, week ending September 20th 2026, covering catastrophe bonds, ILS, reinsurance capital and related risk transfer topics. To ensure you never miss a thing subscribe to the weekly Artemis email newsletter updates or get our email alerts for every article we publish.

item.title: Tower grows first-event catastrophe reinsurance limit to NZ $970m at reduced cost
item.description: Last year, Tower secured first-event catastrophe reinsurance limit of $915 million, which the company said was going to cost it a reinsurance premium expense of 10.6% of Gross Written Premium, down from 13.3% in the prior year. Tower Insurance, the Auckland, New Zealand-headquartered general insurer, has capitalised on favourable reinsurance market conditions to expand its catastrophe coverage again, buying first-event limit of up to NZ $970 million at its renewal, while experiencing improved pricing for the second year in a row. The catastrophe reinsurance arrangements again feature pre-paid reinstatements for two large loss events, while Tower has adjusted its third event arrangements to improve their structure and increase the limit available to $100 million, up from $85 million last year.

item.title: Deploying ILS capital into cyber, AI, data centres requires right fund structures: Albertini, Leadenhall
item.description: As cyber, data centres and artificial intelligence (AI) generate new material cumulations of risk, matching ILS capital to these emerging exposures requires the right fund structures to unlock investor capacity without compromising core portfolio value, Leadenhall Capital Partners CEO Luca Albertini highlighted to Artemis. “Data centres, AI and cyber all generate new material cumulation of risk which will require capital to be deployed. “However, the good news is that the Commission seems to have received the recommendations with a critical eye and there is no implementation schedule and the current expectation is that the Commission may not implement the recommended changes.” Albertini also highlighted the ongoing effort to deploy ILS capital against evolving exposures without compromising core fund mandates.

item.title: El Niño and Heat Fuel Destructive Storms Across Pacific Ocean
item.description: Read more: Highest-Ever Ocean Temperature Measured as Super El Niño Forms Beyond the waters directly affected by El Niño, an ocean heat wave linked to climate change has spread across parts of the eastern Pacific, said Jennifer Francis, a senior scientist at the Woodwell Climate Research Center. A strengthening El Niño is stirring up a dangerous mix of typhoons and hurricanes across the Pacific, fueling storms that have killed hundreds, disrupted trade and caused billions of dollars in damage. Across the western Pacific, that burst of activity has brought a destructive mix of flooding, deaths and economic damage.

item.title: Tech Update: Mosaic Launches AI-Enabled Digital Underwriting System for SMEs
item.description: Mosaic Insurance, the Bermuda-based insurer, launched a digital underwriting system designed to quickly bring complex specialty products to the small and midsize enterprise (SME) market. The new Cyber Tech E&O offering combines HALO’s digital underwriting capabilities with Mosaic’s cyber expertise, in-house claims authority, 24-hour incident response, and Lloyd’s-backed financial strength, the insurer said. Once received, the system automatically structures, enriches, and organizes submission data for underwriting, reducing the need for follow-up questions or repeated touchpoints, allowing submissions to move swiftly, with faster progression to underwriting.

item.title: AI Adoption Is Driving Hiring, But Mostly for Senior Roles
item.description: Companies using artificial intelligence are adding more jobs than those that aren’t, but those gains sharply favor senior employees over junior workers, according to a new study spanning 41 countries. The number of employees in senior positions rose by 6.7% over five years at companies adopting AI, while junior employment declined 3% in the same period, researchers Bharat Chandar of Stanford University and Bouke Klein Teeselink of King’s College London said in a paper released on Monday. Although overall hiring increased, the share of junior workers at those companies fell by 1.9 percentage points, they found.

item.title: EverQuote CEO sells nearly $510,000 in stock
item.description: EverQuote CEO and president Jayme Mendal sold 20,981 shares of the company’s Class A common stock on September 15, according to an SEC filing. Following the sale, Mendal directly owned 591,160 EverQuote shares. The shares were sold at a weighted average price of $24.27, generating gross proceeds of approximately $509,000.

item.title: Tokio Marine-backed WOTA plans water infrastructure council
item.description: Japanese water technology company WOTA is preparing to establish a council to help local governments plan sustainable water infrastructure as populations decline and water systems age. The proposed Water Infrastructure Best Mix Promotion Council would evaluate how existing water and sewage networks, septic tanks, and smaller decentralized water recycling systems could work together. WOTA expects the council to examine costs, maintenance, water quality, disaster readiness, financing, and insurance, with a goal of formally establishing it by the end of 2026.

item.title: Earnix Launches Agent Hub
item.description: (Image source: IIR.) Earnix (Boston) has introduced Agent Hub, a catalog of insurance-specific AI agents and apps within Earnix AIOS , the company’s AI Orchestration System. Agent Hub is designed to bring agentic AI directly into Earnix’s pricing and rating, underwriting and customer engagement solutions, according to an Earnix statement. Earnix says Agent Hub is intended to accelerate execution, improve consistency and auditability, increase practitioner capacity and support faster, better-informed decisions, while keeping humans involved for judgment and accountability.

item.title: Zinnia Adds Whole Life Chassis
item.description: (Image source: Zinnia website.) Zinnia (Greenwich, Conn.) has added a whole life chassis to its Zahara policy administration platform, giving life insurers a configurable foundation for launching whole life products. The chassis is designed to let carriers and distributors configure and launch whole life products in as few as three months, according to a Zinnia statement. We built this chassis so a whole life product launches in a quarter and runs at volume on day one.” Zinnia says the life insurance market is seeing demand for final expense and other small-face products move toward middle- and lower-income households as the population ages.

item.title: FEMA’s New Flood Maps Means More Homes Require Flood Insurance: Cotality
item.description: New changes to FEMA’s flood maps means that thousands more residential properties are now located within the high-risk Special Flood Hazard Area (SFHA), according to a Cotality alert published this week. “Preparation leads to community resilience, which can lessen the burden of recovery.” With flood insurance becoming a requirement for more and more homes in the U.S., it is essential to ensure stakeholders, like mortgage loan providers, forecast future environmental outcomes and assess long-term risk so homeowners aren’t left in the dark on the true costs of homeownership, the alert added. Within more than 100 communities across 12 states, homeowners must comply with the mandate to secure flood insurance within 45 days, or face disruptions.

item.title: Another Tanker Suffers Failure as Crew Suspect Cyber Attack
item.description: A liquefied natural gas tanker bringing fuel from the US to Europe suffered a systems failure that the crew reported as a suspected cyber attack, according to people familiar with the matter. In the latest of a number of potential cybersecurity incidents on tankers, the Vivit Africa LNG was sailing east in the Mediterranean and Adriatic Seas toward Italy early this month when the crew were suddenly unable to access some of the internal control systems, the people said, asking not be identified because the information was not public. Read more : US Tracking Cyber Threats Against Nearly 20 Ships Worldwide After idling off the coast of Italy without discharging its cargo, the vessel on Wednesday began sailing away from its intended destination of Rovigo, heading back toward the Spanish port of Algeciras near the entrance to the Mediterranean, according to shipping data compiled by Bloomberg.

item.title: Equal Parts Acquires Texas’ ProSource
item.description: Equal Parts has acquired ProSource Insurance Agency, a Plano, Texas-based brokerage specializing in transportation insurance. Completed during the first quarter of 2026, the acquisition strengthens Equal Parts’ transportation insurance capabilities and expands its presence in one of the nation’s largest freight markets. Founded in 2003 by President Paul Nhem, ProSource serves trucking companies, owner-operators, commercial fleets, and transportation businesses throughout Texas and across the United States.

item.title: AM Best Revises Outlook to Positive for Oklahoma’s Triangle Insurance Company
item.description: AM Best has revised the outlooks to positive from stable and affirmed the Financial Strength Rating of A- (Excellent) and the Long-Term Issuer Credit Rating of “a-” (Excellent) of Triangle Insurance Company based in Enid, Oklahoma. AM Best said the company has aligned member interests with equity stakes in the company via its Triangle Select program. These underwriting enhancements demonstrate the effectiveness of the company’s ERM, which AM Best assesses as appropriate.

item.title: Gallagher acquires Innovise Business Consultants
item.description: Gallagher has acquired Englewood, Colorado-based McMillan Insurance & Bonding, which operates as Innovise Business Consultants. The Innovise team, led by Jason McMillan, will relocate to Gallagher’s Denver office and report to Bret VanderVoort, head of Gallagher’s Western Zone retail property and casualty brokerage operations. Innovise provides commercial insurance and surety bonding services, with a focus on the construction, energy, real estate and manufacturing industries.

item.title: Sword to acquire Headspace
item.description: Digital healthcare company Sword has agreed to acquire mental health platform Headspace , expanding its AI Care offering beyond physical pain, women’s health and cardiometabolic care. Sword plans to integrate its AI technology into Headspace to provide more personalized support, identify members’ needs earlier and connect them with clinicians when appropriate. Headspace has reached more than 100 million people across 200 countries and is offered through more than 20,000 employers.

item.title: Suspended Glencore Exec Told Radiant ‘Say Nothing on Email’
item.description: A senior Glencore Plc executive last year urged counterparts at Radiant World not to communicate by email, according to WhatsApp messages from the company’s head of iron ore seen by Bloomberg News. Hill was suspended from his duties pending the outcome of a review into Glencore’s dealings with Radiant World, Bloomberg reported on Thursday. “Say nothing on email,” Peter Hill wrote in one WhatsApp message in early April 2025.

item.title: Heat Sears Central US This Weekend as Hawaii on Flood Watch
item.description: Heat will continue to sear the Great Plains and central Mississippi Valley this weekend, as well as pushing into Texas, Oklahoma and even the eastern U.S., prompting the nation’s largest grid operator to call on customers to conserve energy. The combination of high daytime temperatures and warm nights will lead to moderate to extreme heat risk — levels 2 to 4 on a 4-step scale — across large parts of the central U.S. That includes a forecast 71F in New York’s Central Park late Friday, which would come within a degree of toppling a 1972 record for a warm night.
